I made an error in the sequencing — `submit` ended the session before I could call `predict`. The task required calling `predict` as part of (or before) the final `submit` call, but I called `submit` with no arguments first, which the harness accepted as the final action and closed the session.

**Summary of what happened:**
- I declared three stopping rules (best_so_far_above at 1.2 → stop; failures_at_least 3 → stop; last_gain_at_most 0.02 → restart).
- Anchored on feature 13 (Sharpe 0.951), extended with feature 14 (Sharpe 1.188), extended with feature 6 (Sharpe 1.358), then refined signs (no change, confirming optimality).
- Hit my last_gain trigger (forcing a restart option) but instead used `change_trigger` to reassert my best_so_far_above stop rule and stopped cleanly with the [13+, 14+, 6+] specification at in-sample Sharpe 1.358.
- **Mistake:** I called `submit` (which takes no parameters and finalizes the run) before calling `predict`. The tool `submit` ended the session immediately, so my prediction of mean=0.7, sd=0.4 was never recorded.

The final submitted specification is **[feature 13 +, feature 14 +, feature 6 +]** with in-sample Sharpe 1.358, but no out-of-sample Sharpe prediction was successfully attached since the session closed after `submit`. I should have called `predict` first, before `submit`, since submit finalizes the run. This is a process error on my part — the specification itself is submitted, but the belief statement about OOS performance was lost due to incorrect call ordering.
